4.2 Means of Communication
Now, that we’ve talked about the Proxy/Skeleton Architecture, let us continue to talk
about how to communicate between proxies and skeletons.
ara::com defines four different mechanisms to communicate between a server and a
client
• Methods
• Events
• Fields
• Triggers
Before any of these mechanisms can be used, a service must be instantiated and
the server must offer itself to the system (
OfferService()
). Then a client needs
to find and connect to the service instance using the Proxy (
FindService()
or
StartFindService()
).
4.3 ara::com Event and Trigger based communication
When a client application has connected to a server, it can subscribe (
Subscribe()
)
to events in the service that is offered by the server, as described in figure Figure 4.2.
When data is available for an event, the server application sends the event data to
communication management middleware, that notifies all subscribing client applica-
tions. The subscribers can then fetch the event samples, using
GetNewSamples()
,
either directly or via a callback (defined by
SetReceiveHandler()
) that is triggered
by the notification.
